# Draft:RepublicEn.org

Lead Section
republicEn.org is a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization with over 12,000 members that focuses on educating and engaging conservative individuals on climate change issues. It operates under the Center for Climate Change Communication (4C) at George Mason University. Founded in 2012, the organization, led by former U.S. Representative Bob Inglis (R-SC4 1993-1999; 2005-2011), aims to facilitate discussions on free enterprise approaches to climate change.
Introduction
The republicEn membership base is represented throughout all regions of the United States. The organization includes a core staff team and advisors who support members through outreach, education, and media communications. Additionally, an EcoRight Leadership Council, composed of diverse professionals, spreads the organization’s efforts. The republicEn team works on both virtual and in-person opportunities to share how conservative principles can be applied to climate action.
Philanthropic foundations and individual donors financially support republicEn. The George Mason University Foundation processes donations on their behalf.
Purpose
republicEn advocates for a revenue-neutral, border-adjustable carbon tax as a market-based approach to climate change. The organization argues that such an approach can align economic and environmental goals. The group also seeks to bridge political divides in collaborating on climate solutions.
Examples of conservative-led carbon tax proposals in the U.S. include the following bills that have been introduced in Congress:  the “Raise Wages, Cut Carbon Act” (2009), the “MARKET CHOICE Act” (2018), the “Energy Innovation and Carbon Dividend Act” (2019), and the “Stemming Warming and Augmenting Pay Act” (2019), “Climate Leadership Council Carbon Dividends Plan,” and the “Green Flat Tax.”
History
Bob Inglis is the Executive Director and co-founder of republicEn.org. In 2012, along with Alex Bozmoski, Inglis launched the Energy and Enterprise Initiative (E&EI) at George Mason University, a public research university in Fairfax County, Virginia. In the fall of 2014, E&EI rebranded under the name republicEn.org. Inglis received the John F. Kennedy Profile in Courage Award in 2015 for his leadership on climate change. In 2016, he was named to Politico’s Politico 50 list.
Initiatives
The organization conducts various initiatives to engage conservatives on climate issues, including partnerships with universities, student groups, businesses, and other organizations. It uses online and in-person methods to facilitate discussions and actions on climate change. The EnCourage Tour and the ‘EcoRight Speaks’ podcast are among its ongoing projects. The podcast, launched in 2020, features discussions with various guests on climate-related topics.
Past guests have included former U.S Representative John Curtis (R-UT), Climate Scientist Katharine Hayhoe, and Executive Director of Alliance for Market Solutions Alex Flint. The stated aim of the podcast is to highlight optimism within climate news and environmental leadership.
republicEn also organizes in person events, including local field trips and speaking engagements, aimed at engaging conservative individuals and lawmakers in discussions about climate action. Since 2017, republicEn has also been hosting an EnCourage Tour, where Bob and the team travel around the country to attend speaking engagements.
As part of its climate-related communication efforts, the group produces public webinars, a weekly climate newsletter called the 'Climate Week En Review,' and short form content on social media.
Connections
republicEn is affiliated with organizations such as The Conservative Environment Network (CEN), the Citizens’ Climate Lobby (CCL) Conservative Caucus, the American Conservation Coalition (ACC), and the Climate Leadership Council.
